facts.text: Electro-sensitive protective equipment (ESPE) is a family of certified safety sensors, including light curtains, laser scanners and recently radar, that detect a person without contact and trigger a protective stop; IEC 61496 and IEC TS 62998 define how these sensors are shown to be reliable.
facts.quote: ESPE is the family of certified safety sensors (light curtains, laser scanners and, recently, radar) that detect a person without touching them and trigger a protective stop

facts.text: The IEC 61496 series covers general requirements in Part 1, light curtains in Part 2 and laser scanners in Part 3; IEC TS 61496-5:2023 covers radar protective devices.
facts.quote: Part 1 general requirements, Part 2 light curtains, Part 3 laser scanners, and the technical specification IEC TS 61496-5:2023 for radar protective devices.

facts.text: ESPE certification covers detection capability, response time and behavior under faults, and assumes a stationary machine in a controlled space.
facts.quote: Certification covers detection capability, response time and behavior under faults, and it assumes a stationary machine in a controlled space.

facts.text: IEC TS 62998-1 is a newer specification for safety-related sensors that protect people but do not fit classic ESPE categories, including sensors used on mobile machines and outdoors.
facts.quote: IEC TS 62998-1 is a newer specification for safety-related sensors that protect people but do not fit the classic ESPE molds, including use on mobile machines and outdoors.

facts.text: The booklet lists safety-rated sensors as one approach to shortening the safety proof.
facts.quote: The booklet lists safety-rated sensors as one approach to shortening the proof.

facts.text: IEC TS 61496-5:2023 gives radar an established certification basis but explicitly does not consider aspects of a moving radar protective device (RPD) application.
facts.quote: IEC TS 61496-5:2023 gives radar an established certification basis but, in its own words, "does not consider the aspects of a moving RPD application".

facts.text: An unnamed sensor maker claims to have used IEC TS 62998-1 to analyze its radar for mobile outdoor use; the booklet labels this a vendor claim.
facts.quote: One sensor maker states that it used IEC TS 62998-1 to analyze its radar for mobile outdoor use; the booklet marks that as a vendor claim.

facts.text: The booklet concludes that component certification does not deliver system-level performance on a moving outdoor machine.
facts.quote: Its conclusion: component certification does not deliver system-level performance on a moving outdoor machine [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The off-road standard ISO 16001 covers object detection systems with a detection time of 300 milliseconds and continuous self-checking.
facts.quote: The off-road standard ISO 16001 covers object detection systems with a 300 millisecond detection time, continuous self-checking

facts.text: ISO 16001 contains technology annexes for several sensor types but no annex for lidar.
facts.quote: technology annexes for several sensor types but none for lidar [Chapter 3].

facts.text: One school of thought excludes machine learning from the safety function and relies on certified deterministic sensors.
facts.quote: One school of thought keeps machine learning out of the safety function and relies on certified deterministic sensors [Chapter 1].

facts.text: A certified sensor can shorten the component-level safety argument and bound what a learned perception channel must prove.
facts.quote: A certified sensor can shorten the component-level argument and bound what a learned perception channel must prove

facts.text: Sensor certification does not replace validation of the whole system on a moving machine in dust, rain and glare.
facts.quote: it does not replace validation of the whole system on a moving machine in dust, rain and glare.
